Explosives: TNT and dynamite

TNT and dynamite break blocks in a wide circle. Blasted blocks are destroyed, not collected. Creative players can use them freely. In survival, both need Glow crystal, which the world does not generate naturally.

Voxelgame main dd29d91 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Place and light TNT

  1. Select TNT in your hotbar.
  2. Right click a surface to place a whole block. Hold Shift and right click to place one half-metre charge.
  3. Aim at the TNT, within 6 m, and press G.
  4. Step back. The fuse lasts 2.6 seconds.
Key or actionWhat it does
Right clickPlace a whole TNT block.
Shift + right clickPlace one half-metre charge.
GLight the aimed TNT and every TNT piece touching it, even diagonally.
Left clickMine TNT back without lighting it.

Lit TNT pops loose and can fall, roll or float before it blows. Touching pieces go off together as one blast. TNT: place and ignite (G)

Good to know. G does not work on multiplayer servers. The game shows "Explosives aren't available on servers yet".

How far a blast reaches

  • One half-metre charge or one dynamite stick: about 1.5 m.
  • One whole TNT block: about 4.25 m.
  • A touching group of TNT: up to about 10.5 m, which needs about 62 touching TNT blocks.

A whole TNT block cannot break obsidian. Solid stone only gives way close to the charge. Blocks between the charge and a target absorb part of the blast, and water absorbs a lot of it. Explosions: reach, damage and terrain

Careful. Explosions cannot be undone. Blasted blocks are gone. The status line counts cleared half-metre voxels.

Damage and knockback

In survival, players near a blast lose health and are knocked back. Creative players take no damage. Creatures are hurt in both modes.

Tip. Stand well back before you light a group. The blast reaches about 10.5 m from the largest group.

Throw dynamite

  1. Select Dynamite in your hotbar.
  2. Hold right click to wind up. A longer wind-up throws farther.
  3. Release to throw. The fuse starts on release.
  4. Take cover. The stick goes off 2.3 seconds after you throw it, where it is then. It sticks to the first surface it hits.
Key or actionWhat it does
Right click (hold, then release)Wind up and throw a dynamite stick.
  • The stick sticks to the first surface it hits, including walls and ceilings.
  • You cannot place blocks while you hold dynamite.
  • Opening a menu cancels a wind-up.
  • Creative throws are unlimited. Survival uses one stick per throw. A throw that cannot fly keeps the stick.
  • Dynamite does not work on multiplayer servers.

Crafting TNT and dynamite in survival

Tools & arms 2 recipes
RecipeMakesNeeds
TNT8× TNT
  • 32× Sand
  • 8× Glow crystal
  • 8× Boards of any species (Alder, Birch or Pine boards; mixable)

Makes one full TNT block (8 pieces). Needs Glow crystal, which does not generate naturally: the only piece in a survival world sits at the Stone overlook landmark, so this recipe cannot be completed from gathered materials alone.

Two dynamite sticks2× Dynamite
  • 4× TNT
  • 2× Paper screen

Needs half a block of TNT, which itself needs Glow crystal (see TNT).

Good to know. Both recipes need Glow crystal. The world does not generate it naturally, and a survival world usually has one half-metre piece at the Stone overlook landmark. The game places that landmark only when it finds a dry flat spot near its fixed base. You cannot make TNT or dynamite from gathered materials alone. Glow-crystal recipes in survival

One TNT recipe makes 8 pieces, one whole block. Two dynamite sticks need 4 TNT and 2 Paper screens.

What a quit or reload does

  • Lit TNT and burning dynamite are not saved. Quitting during a fuse loses that TNT.
  • Explosions are not recorded in build history.

How this guide was checked
